This game is marked by its most visible flaw - being rushed. The entire ending feels like something put together in a day or two and hastily stitched together. Unfortunately, the stitches don't hold. You are leveling your hero and gaining powers, only to find out that you can only use the more exciting ones during the comparatively brief period you spend in the ending levels. Some storylines are left not unresolved, but simply unfinished and without ultimate purpose and sense of accomplishment. Yes, I know there are "restoration" mods out there, but they were not part of the original game.
Some parts of the gameplay are an advancement over their KotOR counterparts - item modification is more detailed, and the player now gains or loses the affection of their companions. For the majority of companions this ultimately gives an option to train them as Jedi.
Story of KotOR 2 is in my opinion lacking. The main element of the story are the so-called "wounds in the Force", a fan-fiction level of bad excuse for a plot device. There is too much philosophical drivel about killing (!) the Force itself, and the goals and motivations of the player are not always clear. Compare this to KotOR, where the main objectives are very clear - defeat Malak and (learned over time) stop him from using the alien superweapon, the Star Forge.
I am amazed that so many rate this game above KotOR. Storywise, KotOR 2 feels subpar to it. The only reason why one would want to play this is the (relatively) advanced technical side of the game compared to KotOR - customization of lightsabers and other items. If KotOR is 9/10, I would give KotOR 2 something like 6/10. Do I recommend it? Well, of course, if not for anything else, then for informational and historic purposes.

With the next title in the Ultimate General series coming out, I thought it would be a good time to revisit this title. Is it still worth buying UG: Gettysburg? Yes! Ultimate General: Civil War does not seem to be have any scenarios forthcoming for the Battle of Gettysburg, so until some later DLC, this is the only UG title where you can play as either Lee or Meade.  Moreover, the UG experience does not rely upon fanciful graphics or shock value to make the game expereince. Instead, it provides a reasonably accurate but incredibly accessible model of mid 19th century warfare. Positioning is everything. Leave your men in the open in front of enemy cannons, and the enemy will cut them to pieces. Put your men in cover and watch them stand like a stone wall before vastly superior enemy forces. At some point, the battle will come down to a charge. But are your men fully prepared to eject the enemy from a key piece of terrain? Players can get a feel through the "condition" and "morale" rating of their units, but UG: Gettysburg never reveals the full underlying mathematical model, which makes the player experience more like the command experience of an actual Civil War general. The only thing I think the game could improve on is some more clear illustration of LOS and the ability easily reface units (improvements that UG: Civil War has already implemeneted). Overall, UG: Gettysburg remains a simple but innovative design that is definitely worth 15 USD.

"Mighty N*9 is the spiritual succesor of Megaman"
That statement is a lie since Shovel Knight is the true spiritual succesor of Megaman.
Im a huge fan of the Megaman series, and I get a huge feel of said franchise from Shovel Knight. You get upgrades, you get new armors, you fight bosses to progress through the game, you have a red companion and your blue. You also have a helmet.
You might think, "but its just a small game, I cant get my entertainment time out of a game with a megaman style mechanic, their always short" well my dear friend, your free to slap yourself right now because this game is NOT short at all. If your a 100%er like I am, it'll haunt your dreams. The achievements for this game are TRULY a wonder. Ranging from "I can do that!" to "♥♥♥♥ THIS♥♥♥♥♥♥", your on an emotional rollercoaster just checking the achievement window.
Not only that, but you dont only have ONE story. You can play as Shovel Knight, Plague Knight, Specter Knight and soon, as King Knight. And who knows, maybe more in the future. All of these character have their own mechanics and levels, with specific different bosses, all with a well thought out, lore rich story that makes you think on what the developers consumed to get such an amazing creation going. Each playable Knight has a different way to play, so you wont be able to do those shovel bounces with Plague Knight. Maybe he can boost himself with bombs, and maybe Specter Knight can slash upwards, rocketing himself up with his Scythe. but who knows? thats for you to find.
10/10, amazing story, great attention to detail, minibosses, great stage bosses, amazing ammount of weapons and special attacks, lots of easter eggs, lots of upgrades and things to do, bonus stages, special content, tributes to the kickstarters, and most of all, an AMAZING property that you dont see in many games these days. A true passion for making your game as perfect and enjoyable for the broadest possible audience as possible.

This game is a sad waste of potential, just like everything else that comes out of Rebellion. There's a wonderful ballistics model, and the kill-cam is really nice, but the rest of the game is an awful slog. You're given a handful of items, none of which will ever be helpful. Your silenced pistol is too inaccurate to use beyond literally a few in-game feet. If you're hiding outside a doorway and your enemy is on the other side of the room, you've got maybe a 30% chance of hitting his head. You won't want to aim anywhere else, hitting him anywhere else just sets him off. Rocks will trigger enemies, but can distract them for about a half-second. I haven't ever used them because if I'm that close and they don't know I'm there, I'd rather just shoot them with the pistol. I won't touch on the SMG, it's so inaccurate and has so little ammo that they might as well have ignored it. You're better off spamming your rifle, stunlocking with the pistol, or more likely just letting them murder you so that you can restart.
I hear rumors about things known as "stealth" and "flanking", though I've never seen them nor have I ever seen an opportunity for them to manifest. That's not a lack of skill, there's just no other path to take. The first level is within a bombed-out city, which means that there are a handful of buildings you can go in, and everything else is invisible walls and rubble. There is one path winding through the streets, and you have to walk through the open in order to get to the next objective. The first two missions might as well have been on rails for all the freedom you're given. Waypoints and invisible walls push you ever forward, you're never given any reason nor opportunity to place traps on enemies, move bodies you've shot, or otherwise use the level organically. This issue is compounded by the fact that the enemies will spawn in and re-arrange themselves spontaneously depending on your "progress". This means that you'll pretty much never be able to place TNT as traps, you can only trigger them by shooting them. In order to use it as a trap, you'd have to manually place it next to an enemy, then backtrack to a vantage point and trigger the explosives. In lieu of that you could just shoot the enemy from the vantage point and skip the middleman, or sneak up on the enemy and use the silenced pistol. However, the latter option is likely to trigger enemy rearrangements or spontaneous reinforcements as you approach. Enemies are super-eagle-eyed, so you can forget about sneaking around within 100 feet of an enemy unless they're scripted to stare away from you forever until shot. That could change as you get closer, they could spontaneously shift into a patrol route because you passed through an invisible trigger. The awareness indicator is low to the ground, hard to see, and if it's there you've pretty much already tipped them off to your location. This goes double for snipers, who spawn in only when you're about to blindly encounter them, and they are set up so that they will always immediately spot you and engage. If you manage to cheat the detection system through a combination of luck and respawn-based clairvoyance, that still makes them the first target you *have* to shoot in order to progress. On the second level, they're placed so that they can't see you, but that's only so that you can exploit the noise mechanic. The noise mechanic doesn't care about ambient sounds, there's an indicator that pops up when specific events happen (like a train horn), and during that interval you can do *anything* without drawing attention. At all other times, every spawned enemy will hear every shot, and all nearby enemies will track upright footsteps. While enemies are eagle-eyed, they are forgetful. If you're lucky no one has Line of Sight to you and you can wait the minute or so that it takes for all the enemies to assume you've given up and gone home. Be prepared to use and abuse this feature.
My suggestion is to download the demo. If you enjoyed blowing people's brains out, play the level again. That's the level right after the tutorial, copied entirely. It never gets better than that level right there. The maps are just as restrictive, the enemies spawn/rearrange spontaneously in the same "just to F*ck with you" maner, and the objectives are never more than "go here", "plant the thing" or "shoot the guy". I don't blame you for enjoying the shooting, I certainly did. There's just no reason to purchase the full game. No other part of the experience is worth the investment, if you're only there for the shooting than you might as well stick with the demo that lets you shoot stuff for free. If someone's done a Let's Play of this game from start to finish, you should just watch that and be done with it. You can't play this game any other way, the only variable would be your personal shooting performance. To simulate that, I refer you back to the demo.

Arma 3 is a military sim, sandbox game made by Bohemia. Although it is an expensive game, it contains many hours of fun, gamemodes and story missions. It can supply from the minimum of 50 hours - 10,000 (as 1 in 3 people have over 7,000). Don’t rely on the bad reviews about the performance. The performance is good, you just need a good computer. Don’t get a game that is out of your specifications even on the lowest settings because obviously, your game will break and crash and it will be all over the place.
WARNING: I did buy this game in the Arma 3 Apex Bundle in the summer sale but I have never experienced the gameplay that Arma 3 DLCs have to offer as I have mainly only played PUBR and KOTH.
The gameplay offers many gamemodes like GTA (Grand Theft Arma), PlayerUnknown’s BattleRoyale (PUBR), KOTH (King of the Hill), Deathmatch, Survival and End Game. The singleplayer gameplay is bad and not recommended to be played unless you can afford all the DLCs. In the case of people that have not purchased the DLCs, just play the fun part of the game, not the single missions. The gameplay can give you a valuable experince for a long period of time such as 50 hours+. Do not give up on the game 2 hours into the game.
Quality and Settings - The game ran at low frames at first (about 4fps). This is because, most likely, the settings are set to the default which can be medium - ultra. It is recommended to spend about 1 hour going through each setting in depth until the game runs well. I eventually, after a hour, changed the settings so that the game ran at 30fps which is successfully playable. The view settings is a good addition as you can choose between first person (like Call of Duty) and third person (PlayerUnknown Battlegrounds (PUBG is originally a Arma3 mod)). It can suit both a third person and first person player and possibly both at once. The game can also look very pretty and realistic. Also including the realism mechanics that links to to the gameplay.
Overall, this game rated with DLCS is: 10/10
Overall, this game rated without DLCS is: 20/10

Originally played Darksiders 2 on the 360. I picked up the original in a sale last year after being told it was quite different than its sequel. I enjoyed both games, and I think Darksiders 2 definitely improved on the gear system. War has a totally different personality than his brother and makes for a somewhat darker tone in the story. The combat is good and combos work well, weapons feel like they have good weight and a different style than the others.
I'm not a huge fan of puzzles, and Darksiders has a lot of them in both games, if you're frustrated by puzzles in your fighting game you may want to avoid this series, but most areas feature one major puzzle with a few simpler ones, so it doesn't dominate the entire game.
As a word of warning Darksiders is 6 years old. It does not run well on Windows 10 and was crashing just about every other time I alt-tabbed. Save often. Steam achievments are also a little bit broken, as I should have about 80% of them, but only have about the first 5 hours worth. I later figured out that you should restart steam before you launch the game every time, and this will ensure achievements properly unlock.
If you can ignore the slight instability and the fact that achievements aren't working very well anymore, Darksiders is a great game with a fairly long campaign by todays standards (13 hours or so). It has inclined me to buy Darksiders 2 again, for the PC this time so that I can play through it a second time.

LIF:YO - my first review after 18 hours gameplay...
look carefully => it's an early access, alpha...
this means bugs, missing content, crashes, compatibility issues, server wipes etc...
but for an alpha, the game is pretty good developed (compared to other alpha games out there).
the idea / concept is great and has a huge potential, even more if modding will be properly supported!
skills / crafting is not fully implemented, for some this could be a CON...
my PROs:
runs smoothly on highest graphic settings on my Lenovo Thinkpad E530 (!!!)
the game forces teamplay (imo something which has been missing in alot of multiplayer sandbox games)
huge skill and crafting system (reminds me a bit of Star Wars Galaxies)
skill dependencies
increasing, freezing or decreasing skills
crafting dependencies
nice variety of materials and crafted items with quality indicators (related to your skill lvl)
NO ZOMBIES (I'm tired of all these exodus scenarios...)
my CONs:
graphics (gladly it's not as bad as minecraft / wurm online)
alot of servers available, but only a few are highly populated
server connects (between 3-7 mins, maybe more?)
recurring server-lags
alot of time wasted by watching the green progress bar filling up (gathering materials etc.)
fighting is very unwieldy / lumbering
hud needs more attention, i.e. lock inventory / chat etc. on one side of the sceen...
alot of bad reviews on steam (mostly incomprehensible - it's an alpha not a fully developed game yet!!!)
i've read alot about crashes (CTD), but so far this has happened to me only once as i've tried to change my graphic settings to max... so i can't add it to CONs (yet...)
further i can't comment on the patch frequency nor the contents of patches, as i haven't experienced one yet!
and unfortunately i didn't find many servers with high player amounts - i hope this changes over time...
overall...
graphics => 4/10
gameplay => 5/10
skillsets/progression => 8/10
fighting => 3/10
fun => 3/10 (alone), 7/10 (group)
server availability => 4/10
i do recommend this game for people who are long-lasting sandbox/roleplay gamers with a strong drive for teamwork!
cheers and have fun!

As the product description says, SWARMRIDERS (SR) is an endless runner, a shoot em up arcade type of game. You control a bike with 2 person; 1 rider and a 'gunner'. Your goal is to survive as long as you possible can from the swarm (of aliens?)
The Controls, Visuals
Very simple controls. Standard WSAD keyboard and mouse. It supports controller too.
Visually, the entire theme is set in a dark world kinda-feel. So it's dark. The only colors you'll be seeing is white, red stripes from these aliens? (I don't know what to call these because I don't play UBERMOSH) and purple rays from your gunner. And a tiny yellow wording below the bike to show your bike's life. The rest? BLACK. and, and The game engine seems to be running on DOS engine like meaning to say there's PIXELS!
My personal thoughts
How bad can this get right? You just control a bike and shoot off swarm of aliens.
After 20 minutes of gameplay. Switches off the speaker. The Heart pumping soundtrack is killing me.
There is no level progression. There is no weapon/bike/anything to upgrade! There is no story There is nothing! You only control the bike, you shoot off all this freaking aliens swarming on your screen and hope to survive until 1 min 50 sec to obtain 100% achievement and uninstall this product. It's that Simple & Honest. Because there is nothing to keep consumer engage to this product. 2 minute tops product shelf life.
The way I am playing this game is no way near what the product describes: ELEGANT.
I am like a mad man moving my mouse like a maniac. To the point my whole PC table is trembling. FPS RTS RPG RACING games HORROR GAMES SIM GAMES - I've never played until my whole PC TABLE IS ROCKING BUT THIS PRODUCT MADE ME DO SO! ELEGANT?! *vomits more blood*
Don't talk to me about responsive control when I am literally moving the mouse like a maniac.
Ok, controls are working beautifully. No bugs. No glitches. For this, I'll give SR the deserving credit. 60 FPS and my mouse is responsive -my screen is filled with purple lasers-
Now for the rant. 2 things puzzles me..and disappointed me greatly.

I have to ask. Was this design choice intentional? Was it to give players challenge? Was this the best thing the dev could think of?
From the aspect of Design, I am really disappointed. How could you design enemies that attack players outside of the view? That's cheap and unfair - the aliens come in hordes of and they can even outrun your bike. So why is it that you allow them to attack players from top and bottom out-of-the-screen? which is why if you take a look at some of the feedbacks, people are saying this game is more of a luck rather than skill.
On top of that, the aliens explodes on death and release this crazy epic huge smoke (PIXELS!) FOG of WAR that blocks the user view to be able to see how many more swarm are coming. By the time the fog starts to dissipates, it would be too late to dodge.
As a dev, if this is the best you can think of to provide "challenge" to your consumer? You may not realize it but you are shooting yourself in the foot with this 2 design choice. I, for one will remember the horrible experience and I will make sure not to invest in any future product developed by you. I am sorry but take look at steam. There are TONS of indie games. (Some are horrible BUT) There are better product out there with better gameplay, engagement and more fun as compared to SR. What reasons should I support you after experiencing such a negative gameplay experience ?
Now, the next thing I am disappointed is at the steam community who supports this product. While It may be unfair to say so because everyone has different preference but coming from the 2 design issue: it seems the community is open to accepting games that makes enemy attack players outside of the view/fov? This is a dangerous sign. If other developer picks up this idea and start giving us this sort of game..are you really going to support them? Do you really want to see more of this kind of game?
If you answered yes - okay, fine. At least you are aware about the consequences

If you answered NO - then please stop supporting/up voting this sort of games. Stop saying negative/funny description and still upvoting this sort of game. Once the trend picks up, It's hard to hold them back. Look at CS, Dota, king of hills, smite? look at how many variants has appeared?!
My Summary
Do I want to see another similar product on steam? Do I want to go through this sort of gameplay experience? The answer is a simple
. I don't care if a game is FREE or cost me $200. If it has issues, it has issues. A free game does not give warrant itself "to have issues". If that's the sort of mentality people are having - then you should be in "open beta"/"alpha" games where you can feast on ALLLLL the issues you want.
So, on the scale of 0 - 10, my personal rating for SWARMRIDERS is an
score worth 4/10.

Flying Wild Hog does it again.  Lo Wang is back, and it is abount damn time.  In this new installment of Shadow Warrior, there is more of an open world feel.  While the first Shadow Warrior (2013) wasn't your typical corridor shooter, exploration was limited due to the somewhat small maps and I'm not sure if the open world actually makes this game better, but it definately gives you more to do.  Shadow Warrior (2013) had a lot actual game to play for a relatively repetative shooter (I believe it took me 15 hours to beat), and I was perfectly fine with the game length.  Lo Wang's commentary could always keep the action flowing.  In this game, the story and action are broken up with more exploration, side quests, weapon unlocks, and even crafting.
The core of the game is still fantastic, and Shadow Warrior fans will be delighted to know that the combat, which was key to the first game being so great, is still top notch.  If you are not a fan of open world games, don't be turned away too fast.  It isn't a massive sandbox like GTAV.  Think of the maps more like Tomb Raider where you travel between the zones, select quests, and can play through the story at your own pace instead of being forced to go down a linear path.
Overall, I like the game, and it with the 10% off on release day, I can't help but to recommend this game having a great value in regards to dollars spent to content provided.

So I've had Fortresscraft Evolved for a while now and finally decided to write a review. Overall I think FortressCraft Evovled is a great game for people who have the time to sit down for a few hours and play. It combines the addicting factors of base building games with three dimensional mechanics. However that doesn't mean the game is without fault. I wouldn't reccomend playing on a mac as the overall quality of the game decreases. If you are looking for a fast paced game or one that you could sit down for 10 minutes a day and play then this is not your game. In my personal opinion the early game is very tedious until you set up copper and tin automation and even then its still a lot of finding ores, scanning, doing research, etc. Overall, if you are looking for a faster pace game with minimal grinding then this is not for you, however if you are looking for an indepth base building and automation game where there is no best way to do it you found your game.

Let me start off this review by saying I've been following BeamNG since 2012 and bought as soon as the initial release happened in 2013. The dev team has been amazing in supporting and updating the game.
Pros:
Amazing physics, detailed car design, helpful dev team. The maps are absolutely beautiful also.
Cons:
The engine is a small bit unoptimized, but the dev team is working on it. Also, sometimes there is a while between updates but the past few have been very timely, and it seems a lot of background work is behind us.
All-in-all I recommend this game, though it might not be for everyone. A majority of the game right now is a free-roam crashing simulator, though the devs have added a good many situations and races.
Also, this is a state of the art engine. You'll need a fast CPU, and sadly AMD has an architecture stuck in the past. More cores do help, but your AMD will need to be clocked a fair bit higher than usual to keep the FPS other games do. A modern (4+ series) Intel needs about 3.4Ghz to play most of the cars, to keep even the most intensive at 60+fps you'll need 4.0Ghz. Like I said though the engine is being optimized.
On the GPU side you can keep solid 60fps on medium with a 280x, and high will keep you mostly 60 but sometimes into the lower 50s. If you max the game with PostFX and reflections it will drag a 280x into the 20fps range and even a 290x has issues keeping up. This hasn't been as much of an issue until this update, so I'll update if it changes again.
TL;DR smashy, you need a good computer. I rate 10/10

The big gimmick of this game is the infamous kill-cam, which shows you in x-ray vision all the different ways in which you're hurting your enemies. I recommend setting the kill-cam rate to maximum in the settings; it's worth it. The kill-cams are very brutal, sometimes even to the point of making me cringe, but there's something oddly satisfying about watching a bullet tear through the forehead of an enemy sniper and come out the other side, completely destroying the back of his cranium, while being accompanied by the crunchiest sound effects anyone could hope for.
The story is completely irrelevant. The main draw of this game is the combat, and the story just forms the frame that gets you through the corridor towards the next group of enemies. Encounters are set up in fairly small areas, and you decide how you choose to deal with them. Occasionally you can sneak past the enemies, but I usually chose to just kill them all. There are a couple of ill-advised encounters here and there, but for the most part they're well designed.
I chose to play on the Sniper Elite difficulty setting, and I found it to be a fairly appropriate challenge most of the time. There were one or two parts that made me ragequit, but I was well entertained for the vast majority of my ~10 hours of gametime.
Ten hours is a good length for the game; it's not too short, but it also doesn't overstay its welcome. That said, it's that short length that prevents me from fully recommending the game at its full price of 28€. 20-22€ would be more appropriate. Even so, if you don't mind yet another shooter with not much story to it, this would be a very good choice for something to buy during a sale.
8/10

Shooting someone in the eye, whether you hit it directly or through the back of the skull, eventually becomes so common that you barely even notice it. Minimalistic aspect, some pleasant music and a simple but extremely effective concept. A small puzzle game based on music and vectors that will definitely challenge and entertain you.
This puzzle game has a very simple base concept that evolves through progression: your purpose is to reconstruct a song. How do you do this? There are notes flowing from a source point, just like water would do from a sprinkler or a pipe; each source point leaks out notes of a single color and around the screen there are different fans of the same colors. There are also some white circles with an arrow meaning they can deviate the flow in that direction renewing the intensity. The moment you send the note flow through the fan, and this will start spinning, an instrument will start playing. More fans means more instruments. And here's the game. Of course the challenge grows with more colors, with new pieces that can combine base colors into new ones, or can even split the flow. Sounds easy but each "stage" gets more difficult and requires creative directions and positions on the very limit.
A personal note to the developer: the game seems so entertaining yet simple in its mechanics that it could suite well the mobile environments. That could be a neat possibility for the game.
The game is very minimalistic yet effective: black screen colored 2d elements. Simple logos menu, italic fonts for the few words written here and there somehow resembling a music sheet, and it's also relaxing to view.
Songs are very relaxing and pleasant sounding like classical music, some waltz, and similar, considering the rhythm and the use of pianos, strings and other instruments fitting the genre.
The only downside with music is that given the nature of the game you will listen to the same looping tracks for long times, resulting a bit alienating. I understand the fact that puzzle by puzzle you end up rebuilding the song with all tracks but maybe it could be an idea to use different songs, or maybe to make puzzle groups smaller so that the song gets changed more often. Personally I don't feel this way at all, I'm a musician myself, I'm used to looping and hearing the same things while I record, but I acknowledge that this situation could lead to boredom.
Another thing is that when puzzles get more complicated, fluxes are having a hard time to switch their associated fan on, even if they're passing through it without trouble. In one puzzle I didn't use a piece and I had this same problem, I'm not sure if after some time the fan started spinning or it started because I've placed the piece at an irrelevant position (Note to Developer: You can see these situations in my screenshots)
Another note for the developer: there's no exit button to quit the game! XD

Amnesia is an excellent example of a disturbing survival horror game, particularly as the lack of any kind of weaponry leaves you feeling especially vulnerable.
Pros
- It's paced well, taking a little while to get going, almost luring you into a false sense of security, but progressing at a fair pace towards the end.
- It uses sound brilliantly to keep your nerves on edge.
- It doesn't rely on cheap jump scares
- The 'santity' mechanic is excellent: making you reluctant to look directly at the monsters is brilliant as it makes them seem much more intimidating.
Cons
- Getting caught by a monster doesn't feel like a real issue as you simple drop back to the last autosave point with all item/pickup progress you had made, which reduces the fear of them dramatically. The sanity effect is actually more of a deterrent.
- While it's good that the puzzles are reasonably challenging, I was often unsure whether I needed to push ahead or if I had missed something. Being reluctant to trek round creepy corridors, when stuck, I'd feel a real urge to use a walkthrough to check.

When it comes to mind-less FPS violence, I can’t believe people would rather play mediocre games such as CoD when they could just go with legendary classics such as this game. I’m a huge fan of this game, I’ve played it for YEARS, I’ve even been on tournaments of this game and even won two of those. However, I’m gonna try to leave that aside and give you a proper review of why you should or not buy this game, and as usual I will start with the negative parts of it.
...Or I would if this game had much negative stuff. Really, the only negative stuff I can think off have to be Assault maps, as they deviate too much from the other game-modes, and vehicle based maps can be a little weird at times. And maybe that it's multiplayer community isn't that full of people after more than 10 years after release. That’s it!
Instead, what does this game have that it’s good?
First and foremost, the AI. It’s good. It’s really f#cking good. In fact I’m an expert at bugging and breaking games, and rarely I’ve found the AI breaking and falling apart. The game also has the option to put a random difficulty mode and then analyze how well you do against it, then constantly change it so it’s all up to your skill level, something that I don’t think I’ve seen in other games and should be in most of them.
Going right up to that are the maps. Not even one of them feels the same as others, only a few of them grow a bit stale because of them being too big or too small and sh#t like that. The game also has maps from previous games that are memorable, such as Facing Worlds, which is the De_Dust of Unreal Tournament, and even adding remakes and different versions of them.
Another big-#ss point in favor of the game has to be the soundtrack. I ain’t f#cking arround when I say, IT’S REALLY F#CKING GOOD. The devs knew what they needed to make the action feel even more intense, and succeeded immensely.
The gameplay itself is also kind of a master-piece, a one of it’s kind in FPS games. All guns (except the ones to start with) are useful in their own way and have their own flair to themselves. They all have their own ways of being used and are all fun to waste people with, although some need more aim than others, such as the Lightning-Gun/Sniper Rifle and Shock Rifle. And hell, any game that has an Anti-Air weapon turned into a shotgun with a grenade launcher option has to be a great game on paper.
Something that’s also rather unique to this kind of game are the sprees, and the game announcer on it’s own. You know how in these modern fps crap games you get rewards for killing multiple people on a single life? Well f#ck that, here instead you get to hear insane voice clips from the announcer not believing how could you just do what to a human being. From the classic “KILLING SPREE!” to the infamous “HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥”, they’re all memorable. Also, the game keeps track of what you do in a match, and hitting F3 will show you information about it, such as how sh#t your aim is or how many sprees you got in that match.
All and all, is this game worth it?  Did you even pay any attention? Of course it is. It’s WAY superior to the sequel it got later on, which kinda sucked, and it has really good mod support. Infact, games such as Red Orchestra and Killing Floor started as mods for Unreal Tournament 2004, it’s that good. I seriously recommend it to any FPS fan out there who just wants to chill out and have fun murdering anything that f#cking moves. And if you want, install the Bloddy Hell mod, which makes, between a ton of other crap, blood and gore more sadistic and makes it stay on the map forever if you feel so, which is BLODDY F#CKING GREAT.
TL;DR Edition: A classic FPS that never seems to age. F#cking good and cheap. If you like FPS and you don’t have it, you have serious issues either in your brain or your wallet.

Let me start off this review by saying I've been following BeamNG since 2012 and bought as soon as the initial release happened in 2013. The dev team has been amazing in supporting and updating the game.
Pros:
Amazing physics, detailed car design, helpful dev team. The maps are absolutely beautiful also.
Cons:
The engine is a small bit unoptimized, but the dev team is working on it. Also, sometimes there is a while between updates but the past few have been very timely, and it seems a lot of background work is behind us.
All-in-all I recommend this game, though it might not be for everyone. A majority of the game right now is a free-roam crashing simulator, though the devs have added a good many situations and races.
Also, this is a state of the art engine. You'll need a fast CPU, and sadly AMD has an architecture stuck in the past. More cores do help, but your AMD will need to be clocked a fair bit higher than usual to keep the FPS other games do. A modern (4+ series) Intel needs about 3.4Ghz to play most of the cars, to keep even the most intensive at 60+fps you'll need 4.0Ghz. Like I said though the engine is being optimized.
On the GPU side you can keep solid 60fps on medium with a 280x, and high will keep you mostly 60 but sometimes into the lower 50s. If you max the game with PostFX and reflections it will drag a 280x into the 20fps range and even a 290x has issues keeping up. This hasn't been as much of an issue until this update, so I'll update if it changes again.
TL;DR smashy, you need a good computer. I rate 10/10

Business Tour is like Monopoly wit pay to win. You roll the dice and buy cities. If want better results you pay money for rerolls or to roll even, pair or odd.
Pro:
- Good graphics
- Relaxing music
Con:
- Pay to win game! Just check the ranking and you will see that all top players are VIP. You only get VIP when you buy gold for money. For gold you can do rerolls and get other unfair advantages.
You can buy gold with money. In the normal mode you can pay gold to roll again if you don't like the outcome. You can also pay gold to roll even, pair or odd (Pay to win mode.)
It will look like this:
Make sure to play only limited games. Select "no gadgets" in the game settings before you enter game or open a new table. If you don't do this you will be playing an unfair game where the people pay money for rerolls and to roll even, pair or odd (Pay to win mode).
- Most games are with pay to win. It splits the community into credit card warriors (pay to win) and a few players who prefer a game without rerolls and other unfair advantages. Have fun with long waiting times.
A cash shop which affects the game is bad. I don't mind if microtransactions are cosmetics only but if they change the gameplay it is clearly pay to win. You pay money to avoid bad outcomes. You pay money to avoid the city of your opponents. Just pay gold and roll again. This is an unfair advantage you get for paying money and therefore called pay to win.
- You have to view the other players disgusting profile picture the whole time. Some people use naked, disgusting and gross images aa profile picture. Its displayed the whole game. I don't want to see the disturbing picture the whole game.
- Big problems with lags and disconnects. Players get disconnected and replaced by bots in almost every game. You get dropped out of the game for no reason. It is not stabble to play.
- Time is running out before you can finish a game. Why is there even a timer? In the games I played was always someone dominating. Unlimited games are not going to happen.
- People come to your room and press ready as soon as they join. Then you have 30 sec to also press ready and play with only 2 players or you get kicked of your own table. Design flaw! Trolls just enter your table and press ready to start a 30 sec countdown and then leave. At the end of the countdown you get kicked of your own table.
- 2 or 3 people press ready and the last one leaves and the game starts without a full table. People just leave when some players are ready to make them play with less players. The host should be able to start the game. This would prevent a unwanted start without a full table.
- 2v2 is not really a teamplay you don't share the same money or similar. Your teammate is able to buy your city and you won't get any money of him when he does it. You buy a city for lots of money and he just steals it. Without cities you won't earn rent and go bankcrupt. Nice teamplay you have there..
- The player who starts first has the best chances to win because all plots are still free. If he rolls a double the following players have bad chances to win. Starting as the last player is a big problem. The game is over for you before made your first turn. 3 other players started before you and bought all plots. You have to pay them rent and if you want to buy their plot you have to pay them way more than they spent for it. The people who start first just buy the land because repurchase price is really high. You can only hope to reach a free plot or the game will end bad for you.
- The online multiplayer is limited to your chips. Without chips you can't play online. You will either have to buy them for money, play offline games with bots, complete tasks or wait another day to get new ones. Without chips you can't play online. The minimum fee for one game is 100 chips.
The good reviews are from people who pay money for unfair pay to win advantages. No one would like a dice game where your opponent can reroll for money. I can not recommend it. Too many problems, pay to win, disconnects..

As far as RTS games go, this one sounds unique and interesting but ultimately is pretty poor.  You control the forces of either the Union or Confederates and must capture and hold key positions on the battlefield.  Each battle starts off uneven, but reinforcements to each side periodically enter the map.  This means you may start at a disadvantage, having to use guerrilla tactics until reinforcements arrive, and then overwhelm the enemy before they too are reinforced.
It sounds cool, but the mechanics don't actually work in practice.  Attack and movement commands never function as expected.  Units seem to randomly ignore commands to move or attack.  An entire battalion of soldiers can be facing off against an enemy and will suddenly turn and flee despite clearly winning the confrontation.  Artillery units will blatantly refuse attack orders and just sit still, doing nothing.
Movement controls are downright atrocious, often resulting in units organizing themselves in a way you did not intend or desire.  Anytime you issue a move command, the units run around in circles to change from a combat formation to a marching formation.  You cannot tell an entire line of soldiers to fall back and instead much select each troop individually.  The list goes on...
The game leaves you with a feeling of overwhelming confusion.  Why do my units ignore my commands?  Why can't they move in a straight line?  What causes morale and condition to go up or down?  The answers to these questions and more are never provided!

Gameplay Pros:
- The game provides a ton of options for building the automated mining operation of your dreams, and poses any number of real time logistical puzzles for you to solve. If you enjoy design based problem solving of that sort, this is a great game for you.
- Spelunking in the treacherous underworld beneath your base is very enjoyable, with just enough light to make the occasional monster proximity sound very creepy. Expect to do some twitch spins when you hear something sneaking way too close behind you in the ice layer.
- The grappling hook is a blast, except when it murders you by failing in the ice layer.
- The smart help system is a great innovation that should be copied throughout the genre. It considers what you are looking at on the screen when you hit H and sorts your list accordingly. Simple. Genius.
Gameplay Cons:
- The core defense system is very, very primitive, to the point where it just seems tacked on. The only base attacker is a wasp swarm. Not weird alien wasps with tentacles or horns in weird places, they're just wasps. Everything else in this setting is alien and unsettling, then you get attacked by something you have killed in your back yard with a can of RAID. (To be fair, the end game wave is more alien looking, but that is hundreds of hours in for most players, after the normal wasps have already ruined the immersion.)
- The wasps only vary in size and HP. They don't gain new tactics, they don't start attacking you or the cannons or the cannon supply lines. They just fly in the same straight line to the base each time, and shoot slime at it until it goes offline. For 30 seconds, then it is back and nothing has changed. Until you get to end game, there is very little reason to even bother defending the base, unless you are playing on the highest difficulty, in which case one failure to defend will wipe out weeks worth of work by instantly ending your game. There really is no middle ground there.
- The base defense(s) are/is a cannon on a tripod. It changes color as you get higher tiers of it, but it's still the same cannon. The primary challenge of defending your base is keeping the battery charged on said cannon during the zerg wave. That's it. No phalanx anti-air weapons, no rail guns, no tesla coils, no anti-matter fountains. Just the cannon. End game, you can get some missiles, and that's it for your sci-fi arsenal. Cannons and missiles. I do like the defense spider-bot, however. Even though he is automated and requires no strategy or input from the user to function, he is a good example of a cool sci-fi style weapon you might expect in that setting.
-Death by pop-up. It was acceptable when I was playing puzzle games on my Macintosh computer as a kid. In 2017, it just seems lazy. You're walking along and you see a big alien in the distance. You go to investigate the big alien and suddenly a Dune sandworm pops out of the ground and you are dead, with a snarky pop-up to announce said death. No fight, no panicked grab for your rifle, no dodging or strafing, no shield damage or heart loss. Pop, death, Death Pop-up. Start over.
Or you are ascending your newly dug deep core tunnel on your way back to your base when you pass a blue layer of rock in the middle of your flight. You tap your grappler to make the next ascent, but nothing happens. No "cold sensation" or icing warning on the grappler. It just doesn't work anymore. You drop, grappler still does nothing even though you are now in a warm layer. Splat. Death. Death Pop-up. Start over.
Or you get past the Dune sandworm and go investigate the giant alien overmind you saw before. At an unmarked distance from the overmind, but well before you actually touch it... you guessed it, Death Pop-up. Start over.
It isn't to say there shouldn't be dire risk. There must be dire risk for the game to be fun. In fact, I think the risk to your base from the wave attacks should be higher. But this is a game. In playing a game, the "playing" part should be emphasized. There is no game-play element to death by pop-up. Lots of people enjoy the challenge of a good fight, but very few enjoy being randomly brained or splattered with no option to defend oneself.
All of that aside, the logistics puzzles and the spelunking alone make for a fun experience. If you can ignore the tacked-on nature of the combat/defense element, I'd still say give it a try when you see it on sale.

This game is freakin awesome.
The dev is a quirky dude but quirky or not you're a real hero to the indepent developers setting out on their own.  Well done good sir.  Still blows my mind that you did most of this yourself, by yourself.  I know you've had some help along the way but this game is a true triumph story showing it's possible to make something awesome on your own if you work hard enough for long enough.  The fact that you are about the only survival crafting game to ever get out of early access still blows my mind.
About The Game:
I wont re-bother saying all the things already pointed out about how it's like this or that game.  I'll just let you know what I like about it.  To start, It's great for the OCD in me as it gives one the tools to learn what you need without holding your hand so tight that you can't do what you want.  Less about building awesome castles, more about building awesome factories that automate every little task you can think of (Though you can still build castles that like,♥♥♥♥♥♥or even a castle factory).   Best part of this game is when after you've been doing things by hand for hours and finally figure out how to automate the process with logic systems and cool conveyor routes, the reward is a bit like a king sitting on his throne looking out over his land as the farmers and soldiers toil for his gain.  But much less 'slavey' than that sounds because they are all machines.
Anyhow, this game is great for the creative in me and I bet if your easily addicted to fine tuning systems until they are perfect then you'll get sucked into this game right away. I'm 85hours in and still unlocking new tech.  From the looks of what the interwebs has to say, I'll be unlocking things for quite some time to come too.  Not all of it is just the next tier up kind of stuff either.  Research is done in a very creative way as there are two different ways it's tackled.  Early game most of it is just scans, a few hours in you'll build machinse the process cores and spit out research you can use as well. When you finally get a good automated process for it, it's very satisfying.
Anyhow, I've said enough.  I just thought this game specificly desereved some good praise as it stands alone unto all the clones you see around.   I hear a lot of people thinking this is just a minecraft clone but that couldn't be farther from the truth.  About the only thing these two games have in common is voxel landscapes.  Everything else is unique and from what I've seen, completely origonal.  And you can go a LOT deeper in this game then you ever will in minecraft.  Infact, if you go too deep you'll need special heating unit in your suit to keep your♥♥♥♥♥from freezing to death.

I understand there's a lot of skill involved in making some of these jumps, particularly in the later stages, but so much of it FEELS like luck. I don't experience elation or satisfaction when I finish a difficult section, only relief that I'll never have to do THAT again.
The option to only see custom tracks that do not require DLC doesn't work. There appears to be no such thing as a custom track that does not require an additional purchase of some kind. If there is, I can't find it, and the developers surely haven't made it easy to find.

I really don't understand the negative reviews. The single developer has delivered a large amount of content and updates over the years. The game is priced low enough to make the DLC an easy choice to buy (plus you are supporting his efforts). The mod support is great. The game runs quite well considering the incredible size of your bases and world, and the massive number of enemies being hurled at your defenses.
As far as as gameplay goes, if you enjoy resource gather, mining, and automation then this is about the best there is. Even after hundreds of hours I am still sometimes in awe at the massive underground complexes I have stumbled across and built myself. I do agree that sometimes the game can be a bit obtuse in the beginning, but once you understand that things are meant to be built on a grand scale everything gets so much more enjoyable and easy. Also, I will agree that some mods are must haves for quality of life improvements, such as, infinite ore stacks  and Tricky's hoppers.
I know I know, Fortresscraft Evolved has fortress in the name, but where it succeeds most is as an excellent automation and mining game, and you won't be disappointed picking it up as long as understand what it is.

An awesome game. Sniper Elite V2 is a game based in the World War 2 era, and (obviously) revolves around sniping people. The concept of a whole game being a sniper strategy is few and far between to find. An element of stealth is also available.
Gameplay: The gameplay of this game feels great. It feels smooth and slick, and they make the stealth mechanic simple. Controls are easy to get used to, and the game is well optomized.
Graphics: The graphics are really decent in this game, and I can run them on maximum, unlike Sniper Elite: Nazi Zombie Armies 1&2. Those games aren't as optomized as well as Sniper Elite V2, yet it has a lot more content added to the content already in SE V2.
Mechanics: Things like the stealth element in this game feel rather simple, yet when you use it you feel like a professional. If you screw up, the game is forgiving, unlike most stealth games. In other stealth games, you get spotted and you have to "go loud" for the rest of the match/round/mission. In Sniper Elite V2, being spotted is a forgiven sentance, and once you eliminate the remaining opposition that knows where you are (silently), enemies will cease to know where you are and later go "at ease" and act like you were never there.
Storyline: Being unrealistic, I was still interested in the backstory. Some things confused me with the backstory. Since the Soviets and the Nazi's faught eachother, some of them were working together at the same time. The reasoning of the "V2" in the name was V2 Rockets that were set to launch for London and possibly other parts of England. Why the Soviets would work with the Nazis to bomb their allies when the Nazi's were loosing to the Red Army is questionable. But it still felt great to snipe important people in suits.
Overall, the game felt excellent, I like stealth, sniping, World War II, and gore concepts in video games. This game mashes them all together and puts the cherry ontop. I hope Sniper Elite 3 will be just as a success if not better.

The jokes suck,  the gameplay doesn't.
This sequel takes things more in the direction of Borderlands, with loot drops, cooperative play and stat fiddling.   There are a ridiculous number of really creative weapons to collect and upgrade in some pretty unique ways ( triple shot lighting rocket launcher anyone?)
All that said,  It has a few shortcomings :  The writing is a noticeable step down from the previous Shadow Warrior,  Wang has never sounded more tired and lame than he does here.  You don't have to try to turn *every* response into a joke, dude.  Also the graphics are kind of a step down , in particular the character models look pretty chunky and animate like something I'd expect to see in a game from 10 years ago.  I should also mention that it uses a P2P multiplayer framework and the net code is some of the worst I've ever seen, which results in every kind of abomination you could expect (teleporting enemies, getting killed through walls, random disconnects, stuttering,  and absurd frame drops).
Happily none of these issues appear in the single player campaign, and so as long as you're not trying to play with a friend on the other side of the world, you'll probably be fine....  Overall it's a super fun experience and I'd recommend it to anyone who liked the combat mechanics of the first shadow warrior but has a hard on for Borderlands style drop systems.  This game manages to combine both into something pretty special.

A true classic and the benchmark by which all other horror games are judged.
Amnesia is an old school horror experience where it is what you can't quite see that terrifies you more than what you can see. It puts you on the edge of madness and terror and keeps you there without ever pushing you to the point where it because mundane.
The story is actually very engaging, with the protagonist being an Englishman suffering amnesia, stumbling around a dark castle searching for answers. But those answer are unlikely to bring you joy. However whilst the story is horrific enough, the true brilliance of this game is the way it injects you with a feeling of utter helplessness and despair. You never feel like you have any options other than to run and hide, and even those options feel temporary, simply putting off the inevitable for a little longer. And yet run and hide you do.
And no game I have ever played has used darkness so effectively. It is both your best friend and greatest enemy at the same time. It will hide you from the terrors, but it will expose you to the insanity brewing in your own mind. So you flit from light to dark, never able to truly feel comfortable in either.
Everything about this game works well to produce a true feeling of fear. The sound and the visuals are great and the game mechanics are actually very cool. Pushing and pulling items around, moving chairs in front of doors, it all works to give that genuine horror movie experience.
If you like horror games this is a must have. And I dare you to play it at night, with the lights off and headphones one :)

Shadow Warrior 2 is a game about a sarcastic badass slaughtering everything around, including demons, cyborgs, and robots.
My biggest gripe is with the plot, but gameplay is awesome. I split the two up so skip the first paragraph if you want to avoid minor, unimportant spoilers. Some people don't want ANY plot details, so beware I guess.

Plot (Minor Spoilers)  :
The first game (the recent reboot not the 90's one) had a serious plot smothered in sarcastic comments between you and your demon follower, this game however is really just the sarcastic part. The plot isn't nearly as good and the game expects you to somehow know everything that happened between the two games, but there's a huge whole in it. Such as the "Collision" when the demon world and human world collided. We knew demons invaded but when the hell did the Collision even happen? Thats just one example of many. You still have a companion to spew saracasm at, but she is not as fun as Hoji from SW1. The plot isn't horrible, its just average, but it doesn't live up to it's predecessor, which is somewhat disappointing. But, a lot of people don't play games for the plot. Although, there are many many pages of lore you pickup from enemies to read up on, but I didn't see much explaining the world, only characters really.
Gameplay:
Where this game really shines is it's combat. As you continue through the game, you have certain spells, and as you level up you get skill points to enhance those spells. There are only a few spells, namely Force Push, Healing, Invisibility, and the ability to spawn spikes to impale enemies and hold them for a few seconds. Each one has upgrades and enhancements, and you also have sword skills like spin attacks and such that are upgraded the same way. Along with that there's passive upgrades and a whole bunch of skills with usually 5 or so upgrade tiers to spend your skill points on, But the real fun parts are the weapons. There are plenty of entertaining and fun weapons to choose from, including but not limited to: Bows, Dual Blades, Machine Guns, Mini-Guns, Nail Guns, Revolvers, Grenade Launchers, Spiked Knuckles, A Giant Laser Glove, Shotguns, and for those who pre-ordered, a CHAINSAW KATANA. Its pretty fun to use, you can get a normal chainsaw later too, but not the Katana. It kind of has that excitement from Borderlands when you find a cool new gun, but with every weapon that drops.
I amassed maybe two dozen weapons in a single playthrough, weapons drops are very rare, but the how you use a weapon can change entirely depending on what upgrades you throw into one. Each weapon has three upgrade sockets, which you pick up from enemies, which drops extremely frequently, maybe 3+ in a single enemy group. Of course there's rarer ones and common ones, different stats on each, but there's a huge variety of upgrades. There's Stat modifiers, like increase damage, crit chance, fire rate, etc. Next, you have alternate fire upgrades. This can be anything from dual wielding whichever weapon, guided rockets, rapid fire mode (think revolvers,) remote grenade detonation, or throwing your weapon down as an independant turret. There's also elemental upgrades, featuring Corrosive, Fire, Ice, and Electric. You also have a bunch of other equips like amulets, armor, Spell Enhancements, and more. These are mostly for stats and such.
This game does indeed have Co-Op, and you can have a blast with all your friends, planning invisible ambushes, and things. We spent most of the game saying "Did you see that?! I just Exploded/Decapitated/Severed/[Insert Brutal Death]'d that entire group! Very entertaining.
Final Thoughts:
I beat this game in maybe 10 hours, but there's replayability, similar to Borderlands, with a New Game Plus fashion, restarting but keeping all upgrades, gear, and weapons. The combat was super fun, especially with friends, but as a single player experience, the plot was lacking. There's a twist here or there, but nothing special.
Also this shouldn't matter to anyone too much but the fortune cookies from SW1 contained jokes, but in this one 90% of them were quotes from Oscar Wilde. I WANT MY WANG JOKES BACK. I didn't like that change. There's still a few good jokes though, such as "Confucius says a good comic book collection is nature's birth control." or "Wangs Out For Harambe" there's still jokes, but in the first one, ALL cookies were Wang jokes. This is more like a pet peeve than a complaint about the game, so don't let it influence your decision on buying this game.
All in all, I give this game a 7 out of 10. The plot is a 5, but the combat is a 10. It doesn't feel the same as the first one, which is good and bad. BUT, the game is definately worth buying. Even more so for Co-Op with friends.

I initially loved this game.  It was a fun and simple Gettysburg simulator that allowed you to enjoy the carnage of the battle, instead of being caught up in micromanaging regiments and brigades.  However, after a period where I hadn't played in a while, I picked the game back up and noticed something was drastically different.
In the previous version, you could tweak the AI on its difficulty, but generally the units were fairly well matched, the main determining factor of who won each engagement was terrain and morale.
When I picked the game back up, I noticed that even on the easiest possible AI selection, my troops were decimated by the opposing army.  I thought maybe this was a boost to one particular side (I was playing as the Confederates at the time), but when I switched to the Union, I suddenly was being slaughtered by the Confederates!  I would possess the high ground with a Brigade of over +1,500 strong and watch as a smaller brigade of 800 in the exposed valley below would massacre over 400 of my men with a single volley.  It changed this game from a fun experience into a frustrating beatdown where the AI had the advantage in every single scenario.  I went from being able to obliterate the Union on day one in the previous version, to suffering a draw with the AI on the lowest difficulty setting after taking thousands more casualties than they did.  The first day should be an easy victory for the Confederates, that was how the battle actually took place after reinforcements arrived.
Why did you break the game, guys?  This was so much better before the patch, but now it's made it practically unplayable.

The units and controls themselves are simple, but the rest of the elements that are programmed into it really make the game very complex. Unit morale, the effects of flanking, charging, cannon fire and fatigue, along with terrain advantages etc. The many elements that are avaiable to use are really what you should look at in this game, those are actually more important than your actual units most of the time.
Its not really a build a bunch of units and match them toe to toe attrition style game that we have now days. Where units are specifically designed to be strong against other units in a sort of fancy rock paper scissors game. This is more about manuevering units, taking certain terrain features and recognizing weaknesses in enemy manuevers and positions and exploiting them.
If you have played sid meirs gettysburg and liked it, then pick this one up and get to it. Very very similar and I think you'll feel right at home.

A pretty fun take on the classic Monopoly where games run a lot shorter, a timer of 30 minutes is up for normal games (and there is even a quick match option for 15 minute ones) if the timer runs out the player with the most profitable empire wins.
There are daily challenges in the game, that reward you with chips (a currency you bet with other players in games, and is tethered to a ranking system for best players) and the challenges can give you small booster items in game like only roll evens, or just odds, or redraw that chance card (these small advantages can be disabled when making a match in online mode if you'd like a super fair game). For 3 bucks in the game you can earn paid cosmetics from these daily challenges, interesting dice with different colors and themes that you can roll out in online games and prove to your opponents that you are the fanciest of all.
Winning the game is a bit different than normal monopoly as, if you get all of one type of property you get a monopoly, and 3 of those you win right then and there, same if you get all 4 resorts (trains) or manage to buy an entire line of the board, other than that, bankrupting your opponent is always still an option :)
Theres a nice tutorial that fills you right in nice and easily without holding your hand for too long, and there is an option to play against the computer if you're fed up with real people, or just want to practice your skills.
Menu navigation for the game is very user friendly, achievements on Steam reward the players who keep playing, microtransactions here dont give any real advantage (as long as you play games with gadgets disabled), tutorial is great, you can play 1v1 up to 4 players against one another, play 2v2, invite friends to your games, or even just play with AI, or with fam or friends on the same computer :)
A few additions would be nice for the game, like being able to play a single-player match while waiting for your online matchmaking, maybe even something along the lines of guilds or an event mode that mixes up the board would be really fun.
The game is a shorter version of monopoly, games have timers that keep it under 30 minutes (or even 15) and you can win in different ways. Paid stuff doesnt give an advantage over normal players, which is fairly important in my book, and you get fancy cosmetic dice if you want to give back to the developers. You can play this one with AI, with peeps around your house, 2v2, 1v1 up to 4 players battling, the whole enchilada of player versus player fun. Daily tasks are fun to achieve, boxes you can sell on the Steam market place for a few cents. And the game is super awesome! Its free to play so why not give it a go?

It's a strangley satisfying experience watching a car get crumpled into a million pieces. If you have ever played Next Car Game (Wreckfest) then you'd probebly expect this to be very similar, but in all honesty, this is unlike any other physics engine I've ever layed my eyes on. The physics in Next Car Game are hard, and almost given an arcade feel to them, but BeamNG focuses more on realism. Granted some cars can feel a bit slow and lethargic at times, but for me, I'm not exactly bothered by that. If you ever get bored with the game itself, I recommend downoading some extra content for the game (mods). It can sometimes add a whole new depth to the game. When you want to do more that crash into stuff, check out the challenge minigames and push some of the cars to the limit, and even if you fail, you can usually see your car smash into something, which is nice. All models are creativley designed, and each one drives differently. You can also drive and shoot a cannon, which I feel is worth mentioning. Do note, this game takes LOTS of computer power to run if you're looking to play on some pretty decent graphics, but all and all, this is the ultimate driving simulator. (Sorry Gran Turismo)
Pros:
-Fantastic Graphics
-Addicting and fun crashes
-Weather system (Change they time of day, or the weather at any time)
-Realistic driving

-Fan-made downloadable content (There is no Steam workshop. You have to download these mods off of the BeamNG website)
-Interior View
-Fun little minigame challenges
Cons:
-Takes a lot of computer power to run.
-NO multiplayer
-Very derpy local multiplayer (Yes, there's local multiplayer, but it's in an experimental state at the moment).

The pros: Beautiful board, and fairly addictive gameplay that's pretty easy to grasp. Bears repeated playing.
The cons: The damage calculation is embarrassingly bad and slanted heavily in favor of the A/I. A single battery of 120 troops (6 cannons) is somehow capable of routing a brigade of 1,200+ men in a stand-up fight - as if that ever happened in the actual Civil War. A/I infantry brigades are virtually unbeatable head-to-head no matter the numerical superiority and can lose 90% of their men without routing. I've won the battle multiple times and NEVER lost less than the A/I. The artillery is also frustratingly hard to use effectively - sometimes they'll be unable target an enemy unit directly in front of them, despite no obstructions. It's also kind of weak the units go no smaller than the brigade level.
On the whole it's a lesser version of Sid Meier's Gettysburg - better looking, but the engine is nowhere near as good.

It starts so well, it is like Factorio or similar factory/base building games, but being in 3d makes it a lot more exciting. The problem is that after a while, you have the basic factory and there is nothing else to build. You do unlock some more objects but they are crafted in a moment and then placed and then you are done. So you are adding occasional new little machines or boxes, but you aren't actually building a base, and you certainly aren't building a 'fortress'. There is really no fortress or base building at all, you just build a basic factory, and then instead of tower defense, you just build 4 lasers and put one in each corner of your base and it kills everything. Later you need to upgrade that by adding a rocket to each corner but you will complete the game like that. There is really no tower defense gameplay in here, no shaping the paths and no multiple tower types with synergy etc. It is just a line of flying monsters that head straight to your core and get killed by lasers when you aren't even there. And even if they don't die, it doesn't matter because there is no penalty for them killing your core. It just regenerates and is back to normal 2 minutes later.
The game seems great at first, but it all falls apart after a while and you see how under developed the whole game is. I suggest getting Factorio instead because although that game is 2d and doesn't have the exploring and digging for resources, the actual factory building is more fun, more balanced, and less of a micro management chore. Also the combat is more promising because at least you have to fight back in that game. Also there are a more and better mods, including one that lets you fight back with planes etc. FortressCraft has some mods but not many, and most of them don't do much. You might get a new storage box or something but there isn't anything that adds anything significant to spice up the gameplay.

This game is probably one of the best games ever to me personally. It is one of those games that to this day, has aged well. There are signs of aging sure, but mostly due to issues with newer OS (Please fix Creative, thanks!).
This game pits you as one of the three Ancient Roman families against the world, destined to conquer and divide and while only the three initial Roman families are avaliable at the start, if you completely conquer certain nations, you can unlock those too for the Grand Campaign.
What makes this game great is the amount of randomness and innate customazable characters that give this game personality. Through the family tree you will gain members and depending on how you use (or not) them, they can become crazy warmongers or glorious leaders, a depth Creative Assembly never truly tried to recreate after Medieval Total War 2. You will care (or hate) these characters as their personalities shine during their grand speeches before your army clashes with the enemy.
I recommend you this game, not for its combat and action, but for its personality and charm. Each grand campaign will likely be unique as different nations rise and fall and different characters are born into your family. If you haven't tried it and you love turn based/RTS strategies, don't miss this one out.

For the first two hours, I loved this game - the killshots are cool, and using wind direction and gravity to aim is a blast.
However, I have two big gripes with this game.
1: Enemy Snipers
This is at the top of my list, because they are downright infuriating. No spoilers, but at one point, you're tasked with eliminating a sniper team. Sounds pretty cool, right? If you've seen the movie, "Enemy at the Gates", then you're probably expecting something pretty epic. Well, don't.
Instead, expect insta-spawn snipers who will lock onto your position with impunity, and rarely ever miss. Rather than a game of cat and mouse, it becomes a battle of memorization: "Okay, once I cross this point, a sniper pops up in that tower".
On higher difficulties, enemy snipers will cause you die in two shots, and because they have a quick reload and 99% accuracy, you'll die. Alot. And not in the Dark Souls 2 fun way.
2: Enemy AI
I briefly mentioned this with the talk of enemy snipers, but the spawns in this game might have you throwing your controller. As stated previously, there is no dynamic AI. Instead, it's based on you crossing a threshold, or killing a certain number of enemies. That's not a sin in itself - alot of games do that - but the way this game does it is just punishing. You'll advance through a section stealthily, only to have a squad of soldiers spawn behind you and gun you down in seconds.
2a: Stealth
This isn't really a point, but don't expect to go through this game stealthily. While you do have a single-shot silenced pistol, the game will essentially force you to go loud in every encounter.
---
To be fair, on lower difficulties, this game could be a fun game. I'm one of those guys that likes to jump on games at the hardest difficulty, because I like to be challenged. This level of difficulty isn't challenging, though. In Dark Souls,  I'm getting increasingly better at the game each time I die. In Sniper Elite v2, the difficulty comes from memorization.
When the game works, it's awesome. There are moments where you actually feel like a badass sniper, and it's fantastic. But, those moments are usually sandwhiched in between "I hate everything" sections.

Basically Minecraft with techmods without all the weirdness that comes from Minecraft with techmods (pickaxe into nuclear reactor, what?).
It is very addicting to automate everything, but this is not all. This game has also tower defense elements, as you have to protect your base and certain buildings from regular waves of enemies with turrets and proper logistics, to keep them working.
Sadly the game also has some drawbacks. Especially the depth of the map is annoying. Just getting from T1 to T2 ores needs you to dig hundreds of blocks down which also means you then have to create ways to transport energy down, ressources up and a way for yourself to get fast up and down. And this game has actually four tiers. There are ways to make this easier, but those arrive quite late (e. g. a quarry that digs a 3x3 shaft down so you can immediately use a elevator).
Also the tech tree is quite weird at times. For example, it takes hours till you are able to use mincarts and when you have them, you simply don't need them anymore.
The game has also some technical issues. The UI is ugly as hell (and feels like it is done for a tiny resolution) and the draw distance is quite low. Also items on conveors are invisible regulary.
Other than that it is a fine game if you like fiddling around with machines and automation. It is better than Minecraft with mods in that area.

A piece for those who miss and/or don't have access to the real horses.
Overally nice game for family and kids, but the price is way too high for what game offers now. It looks pretty nice and has nice atmosphere, it has some quests and a free ride mode with a huge enough territory for a ride and exploration. Calm game for mood and scenery - no action, no harm in any ways, no horror surprises, no damage. Just riding. Only war that can be here is with the textures at some places (and only in the case when you try to get there where you're not supposed to be).
1) Characters are well-drawn (in statics) and well-voiced. But that's a completely static art. Only character that is animated - the horse and some other animals that you'll met in the game, but can't say that there are much of them.
World is beautiful, too, but on low graphic settings some places better not to count at all.
2) Maybe it was at the start placed as just riding/caring game, but here is some kind of a situation where developers took already existing story and characters, so game is - or looks like - kinda story-based... but it has no actual storyline. No, I don't count quests like "collect this", "find that", "catch that" and etc as a story beyond existing story, especially when one quest actually repeats another and just points some situations like lost apples and books, and a runaway cows. So point "
, bump into old friends and discover the locations mentioned in the movies and books" is not actually true. We have some scenes and dialogues, but basically all the game is about riding and racing. And horsecaring. And all.
You do not have actual gameplay of Mika. You just control the horse... or ride the horse, to say better. Worse thing is that I've took a long free ride before finishing the quests... to later run in the quests to the same places. You'll not see anything new in this case.
I can agree that races are fun enough. But the game do miss some more full and interactive storyline.
3) Poor animation. Well, I've read all other comments, was thinking a lot, so I've actually knew what I'm taking and was quite ok with it. I miss tranings and lessons IRL, as the horses I've worked with, and this game could be something good for relaxing at the evenings. And it is...
. Yes, I can believe in sprint, I can believe in walking and the trot, I can believe in jumps, but Ostwind's (or Windstorm's) movements on gallop are just completely unnatural. It looks like he's always running through some obstacles even when you're actually running straight on the horyzontal road. It took me long enough to understand what's so wrong with this, I've pulled up my memories and some vids, then I've realized that horses are just moving a little bit differently from other animals, with different rhytm. Especially with a human on their backs.
Model also turns while like still running straight. No even basic horse's reactions on turns.
If count in mind that game is actually all about riding and racing and don't have any other ways of gameplay, yes, I was seriously dissapointed by that. Because it IS ruining all the atmosphere and always stucking in mind when you look at it not from the Mika's back and gives permanent feeling that something is wrong.
And makes me feel that at least the only animated model could be done at high quality. But it's not.
And because of that I'll hold on my opinion that it IS overpriced. Thought I'm not hoping that the devs will fix this animation since it looks like that not all the players are bothered with it.
Other thing is, that after some time horsecaring process becomes annoying. Good point that before/after rides you need to keep Windstorm in a good state, but no need to compare the game (no animal interaction) with no chance after all the quests (!) to avoid this, and the real life.
Gameplay by quests also is short. And, as I've said, modes and tasks are repetitive.
In a few places you can actually get stuck in textures.
And yes, I realize that this game is more for kids and kept this in mind while writing overview on it. I enjoyed my time playing it and still can reccomend it for people who loves things like that and who loves horses, and can be ok with all the described cons. But I recommend to take it on a discount. It's just my overall impression was ruined mostly by the weird animation and I can't agree that all is OK and perfect here with it for a price like this.
