Thanks to the TSL Restored Content mod, which is a definite must-have for Knights of the Old Republic II - The Sith Lords, I'm able to finally give KotOR 2 a 10/10. This series has reserved itself its place in video game history with an awesomely presented story, which especially in KotOR 2 is presented in a much darker fashion than one would be used to from a Star Wars installment, and excellent round-based combat and an abundance of decisions the player will make, each of which with their own consequences, each of which shifting your hero toward the Light, or the Dark. Both are fun, both should be played.

Honestly, I can't say that this game is all bad. It did have it's moments (I bought it for console originally so I have about 50ish hours logged there as compared to here). But, long story short: If you want a game that is a full release yet feels like an alpha release, be my guest and buy it. Otherwise, don't. The controls are a bit odd and hard to get used to. The dialog is, quite frankly, stiff and unemotional (especially for an RPG). And while this game may add some very cool concepts to the gaming industry, it does not deliver as it should. Oh, and don't even get me started on the tutorial that takes around an hour (or more) for most people. And that most of the "map" is completely unavaliable for you to play on (and I mean the non-tutorial actual game map).
Overall, it is not worth a buy. Not even on sale. But, if you want to, buy the game and see for yourself. As I said earlier, I have 50ish hours of this game logged into my console. It's an interesting romp in a strangely unfinished world. This game HAD real potential. I only wish that it was fulfilled.

This game was pretty fun. On the positive side, I really love the adorable art style and the smooth controls and gameplay. The goal of the game is similar to that of a basic runner game, where you run, from left to right, jumping and survivng for as long as you can. You collect as many points as your can to spend on new skins for your dog to change their appearance.  I really enjoying how simple, yet challenging the game is. If you spin in the air by hitting a banana, you can knock out certain enemies. However, keep in mind that the enemies will return for vengeance, much like the chickens from LoZ.  The game also has a lot more little tips and secrets, like this one, to give you an edge in lasting longer.
On the downside, I really wish there was more to this game. I would have liked to see more skin options, new levels, and more game modes. However, this is a minor gripe, as the game itself is very well done; and I find its simplicity to be strangely appealing. It is a great way to kill time while waiting for your friend to get out of the shower; and overall, it is well worth the low price.

Here are the things that I like about this game:
1. Mastering a class (or all of them) is extremely rewarding for the player. This feels so good because the player feels more rewarded while playing.
2. Acquiring new items or cosmetics can give new players a boost of confidence to keep playing. Long-time players can also have this feeling if something valuable is unboxed.
3. The multiple game modes provide a better sense of the overall structure of the game. In Mann vs. Machine, for example, players can hone their skills without as much competetion from players who have more skill than they do.
4. Casual Mode is a great oppertunity for new players to get excited and veterans to chill down and have a fun time after long hours of grinding and competitive mode.
5. While playing the game, one feels like they are immersed in world that has been created with love and great detail. There are also many kinds of playing a certain class, such as the Demoknight (a sword-wielding Demoman with a shield).
Things I dont like about this game:
1. The learning curve is steep for new players, which could turn some of them down from picking up the game full-time.
2. Team Fortress 2 is unlike many other First-Person-Shooter titles (such as Call Of Duty or the Counter Strike series). This is also something that may turn new players away because the game is hard to pick up right away and be good at. Sometimes the game can be frustrating, as players will need to go through many stages to try and get better at the game.
So, I leave with this:
Team Fortress 2 is a great game for people that want something new in the FPS genre. With it's cartoony style and movements, the game can be very rewarding. While starting out may be difficult, the more and more someone plays, the more fun it will get.

Guys. I'll admit it. I used to hate Team Foretress 2. I wanted to like it but couldn't. Then, a few sundays before writing this, I gave it a second chance. AND ADORED IT! Scout, a very fast runner who whoops anything in his path. Soldier, who can fly into the air and rain down massive damage. Pyro, a destroyer of people with afterburn damage. Demoman, a bomber of massive proportions with many grenades and bombs to choose from. Heavy, the mascot (I think), a durable tank with heavy hit rate. Engineer, a handyman with many talents, teleporters, turrets, and dispensers, as well as a variety of tools to club your enemies. Medic, my personal favorite, a healer with some good attack and a swell gimmick with the Ubercharge. Sniper, is self explanatory with some rage included. And Spy, we can't forget him. He is stealthy with many forms of espionage and stabbing. Of course I would recommend it. It is free so go add it to your library and give it a try!

Despite so many negative reviews I also agreed with (according to gameplay videos) ,  I decided to buy this game after Update 1.3.9505 . So, this review will be based on that update.
------------------------------------------------------
After first few hours of gameplay, I kinda enjoyed, but as an arcade , still-buggy-af game; not as a simulator. This GAME is a disgrace of simulation genre in this state. I will explain the MOST IMPORTANT BUGS/ERRORS.
MAJOR 1 - PHYSICS - SYSTEMS :
No matter what graphics it has (No matter if Unreal Engine or OMSI-Like simpler graphics from early 2000s) , in order to call a game as a simulator, it DOES HAVE TO have realistic physics as priority. In Fernbus Simulator, it is exactly the opposite.
There is no sense of weight, gravity, and effects of ground conditions (dry/wet/icy). You can accelerate at exact same rate when climbing %50 grade , and when descending it. Totally arcade, and this is the exact point where this GAME really spits on Simulation genre by carrying the "Simulator" title in its name.
The acceleration and handling of bus is sub-par . Automatic gearbox simulation is severely arcade-ish.Even at cruising, it always upshifts at same high RPM (Remember from racing games) , and skips gears senselessly. Manual mode - 3rd/5th gear rolling mode does not work at all.
Tilting of bus... Lol, I bet the scripters of this game have never ridden in a coach before. Realistic tilting setting makes the bus tilt like no tomorrow, and the actual real setting is called as "Driving on rails" . As a long-term commuter who had driven on coaches more than 1000 times in real, Driving on rails setting is the real one.
MAJOR 2: OPTIMIZATION
How can a game give less fps (loss by %50-60) in less-populated roads than major cities like Berlin?  I was getting like 35-40 fps on my i7-6700 and GTX960 in Berlin, then suddenly dropped down 10-15 in autobahn. Something really buggy here.
Even at maximum settings, the game won't look as good as expected, solely on in-game settings. You may need to enhance it by Nvidia Inspector / AMD Control .
MAJOR 3: AI
AI is cancer of this game,literally.  They will keep stopping at green signal for no reason at all, even at autobahn junctions.  They will undertake you even on autobahn, crash into you carelessly, test 100-0 braking randomly, and block the junctions because they are too stupid to drive on the road properly; causing you to waste minutes / drive over pavement...
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
OVERALL: Do not buy this GAME "at this state". This GAME is still not finished, doesn't feel like SIMULATOR at all, and EXPENSIVE for what it offers. Maybe they will be fixed in short time, but if you look at TML Studio's previous games (World of Subways series, Bus Simulators) you should keep your hopes low, because they were still arcade and dissatisfactory after updates...  Wait for major sales to buy this for trial. Otherwise, wait for LOTUS Simulator by Marcel, and Euro Coach Simulator by SCS Software, which will make this GAME look pathetic.

First time I am writing a review here for any game! This is actually the first game where I really felt a compulsion to do so xD
I'll start with a simply pro and con list for a quick reference of what to expect, before I write a bit more about it:
+ lots of puzzle solving and planning ahead
+ game occupies your head even when not playing it (a rarity)
+ great sense of accomplishment when you see a personal project finished or succeed (I cheered when I saw my first Cargo Elevator come up fully loaded with Iron Ore, unloading it all on conveyors towards smelters)
+ graphics (may sound odd for a voxel-based game, but on the higher settings it has great lighting effects
+ a good intuitive 'rule-system' (the first 5 minutes is a tutorial which shows the very basic controls, but after that you will have to figure out all the rules on your own mostly, unless you want to be handheld the entire process by reading wiki's every 5 minutes. The ingame help encyclopedia (H) gives you just enough information at times, but doesn't give everything away thankfully).
- Occasional bugs (I only remember falling through a lift at times, or a lift only going up to 32m instead of 64m, though that was because I was playing the game on low-end pc at the time instead of my regular pc, if I read some comments correctly)
- Occasional freeze (mostly when doing multiple Coloured Ore pings too rapidly, probably my processor not being able to handle that though?)
- Annoyance of the constant wasp attacks, where at one point I simply stopped building Threat Reducers since they required too much power compared to what they delivered. Besides, the penalty for not killing the wasps was absent, you only lose your command module for a minute which didn't bother me that much, since most of my power came from other devices which were not affected by the Wasp attacks.
In short: Fortresscraft Evolved is an amazing game, really. I never played it's predecessor or any other 'Minecraft-clone' as people sometimes refer to these kind of voxel based games. But really, from all the MC vids I have seen, FCE really adds quite a few layers to that formula.
It's been a long time since I played a game that has me thinking about it almost the entire day long. 'How am I going to deal with this or that', 'What am I going to do next?', 'What's my next project going to be' are questions that occupy my mind the entire time, even during work or on the train home :D Now, that's the sign of a great game, if you ask me.
Apparently I actually bought this game during Early Access phase, but wasn't really impressed at the time (mid 2014). I only tried it out recently and it truly feels finished right now (and yet still it gets regular patches, the developer actively approaches the community for new ideas, etc.)
I think the best way to express why this game is so great is through a few examples, instead of writing too generically about it. Basically the entire FCE adventure is a constant chain of small puzzles that need to be solved in order to continue:
Last night I had just dug a second shaft towards a Lithium deposit, right next to an older shaft which had a Iron deposit I was already mining and sending upwards using a cargo elevator. These two shafts were only separated by a wall of 1 voxel wide. Within this wall I had also dug a 1x1 voxel wide column downwards to place the Laser Power Transmitters to send power deep into the earth (like the name says: these devices spread your power/electricity to remote places easily). However, this second shaft was right in between the bottom of the first shaft and the horizontal tunnel where I was mining the Iron. In order to keep supplying power to this horizontal tunnel whilst also delivering power downwards into the second shaft I had to fiddle around with batteries and Laser Transmitters in such a way that these devices were not in the path of either elevator shaft, yet still were in sight of the ore excavator at the end of the narrow Iron Ore tunnel. The solutions are often numerous, but each has it's up- and downsides. 'Do I dig an entire new shaft upwards just for these Laser Transmitters?', 'Do I widen the Iron Ore tunnel so I have more space for the batteries/Laser Transmitters to place inside the wall between the two elevator shafts?' or do I simply abandon the project altogether and find a new place to mine Iron.
The answer to that last question is almost always: 'NEVER!'. You always want to find a solution, constantly analyzing the situation, figuring out the most efficient and best way to solve the numerous puzzles that you will be facing. And the beauty is: these puzzles are not bound by any hard limits (like most puzzles games, where you have 'levels' that you need to solve to proceed to the next) but they overflow in each other; the solution to one problem brings an entirely new problem with it! Or it might solve multiple problems at once!
Also very important to acknowledge: You create your OWN puzzles! Everything you face is your own doing. You were the one that dug this shaft here. You were the one that decided to mine this Iron vein instead of that Iron vein. You were the one that decided to place certain machines too close together so that when you had to expand your base you ran out of room for lack of planning.
I could name more and more examples, but I think the above illustrated perfectly the feeling you get when playing this game. You either crave that sensation or you don't (basically if you have a logical, analytical mind you enjoy this game, if not...  stay away :P ).

I feel that some of the reviews are unfair for this game. I've amassed nearly 30 hours in this game now so I wanted to give a balanced review.
Overall I really enjoy this game. If you like driving simulators like Euro Truck/American Truck Simulator then you'll love this game. The map is expansive and you really can get lost into the driving for hours. The cities are large and feel very realisic. I really enjoy getting out of the bus to check in the passengers and think that this adds to the immersion of the experience.
XBOX controllers do work (partially). You can drive and operate most of the ancillary controls but you still have to use keyboard and mouse for check in and working the wipers.
There are no pre-set routes in the game but the official Flixbus website is really useful to find real routes that you can drive.
The game is not without flaws though. Hopefully some of these will get worked out with time. Optimization needs to be improved. The game is beautiful to look at but even on low settings sometimes runs with low FPS.
AI - this definitely needs improvement. Cars will stop randomly on the Autobahn or slow down to 30km/h in the fast lane. Cars don't merge properly at lane drops or slip roads. Cars will sit for ages at green lights and then move just when the light is about to go red (very annoying), despawn or sit and block up the middle of junctions. Maybe, like in OMSI, the devs could add an option to disable AI collisions until the AI has become more accurate?
I would recommend the game because in spite of all these things I still find it an enjoyable game to play.

Here's my overview of this game:
- There's no damage drop-off for weapons in this game so someone can kill you across the map with an SMG
- The jumping in this game feels choppy as if the guy is hitting his head everywhere he jumps
- The models in the game are low quality despite having highest visual settings
- The maps are not well optimized and can have lag on hardware well over the recommended requirements
- Some maps fail to load in multiplayer leaving all participants in a frozen lobby
- The game attempts to emulate Call of Duty in some aspects (running, player classes, interface layouts, etc...)
- Little to no gun recoil action, so it becomes a literal point-and-click game
- Poor netcode, 30ms latency when hosting a game and on an Ethernet connection
- Not a lot of options for weapons and customization
- Not a lot of players in this game
- Takes up too much disk space for such little content
The only thing this game has going for it is the fact that it is free to play.

I really wanted to like this game. I really, really did.
As once-upon-a-time veteran of the ages old Firaxis game, Gettysburg!, the predecessor that this game OH SO CLEARLY rips off, and seeing the good reviews for this one, I snapped it up as soon as I learned it existed.
Mistake. See last two paragraphs for TL;DR
The AI is good...I guess. But the controls and responses of individual units are clunky as hell and uninspired. Cripplingly so, in fact. I can barely even make it past the first battle without something random happening to my units that isn't my fault. I'm not talking about morale breaking (get to that pile of bullcrap in a second), I'm talking about painstakingly arranging my lines to have them deform and shift for no apparent reason, and in this game, that kind of nonsense loses battles.
Example 1: Skirmishers and the Vidette's on the Union side act like garbage. You'd think mounted ranged cavalry and light foot marksmen would know how to chase down a marching enemy and shoot them on the move. Apparently not. Told three groups of skirmishers and two groups of videttes to engage a regiment marching for Oak Hill.
Not one of them fired a single shot. They all just faffed about, well within firing range, jitterbugging around. Morale fine, reload fine, LOS fine, I paused and I checked to confirm. This is not the first time this has happened.
In fact, the unit handling seems to generally just be♥♥♥♥♥♥ And that's putting it kindly. Where the AI brigades will turn and wheel snapily, my brigades sluggishly pivot, not firing, as the AI jukes, maneuvers, and out flanks me with ease because their soldiers aren't acting like sea-slugs with chronic narcolepsy.
Example 2: Not firing at greybacks marching up your♥♥♥♥♥seems to be favorite thing of Union soldiers. They will often refuse to automatically engage enemy brigades coming into range. Posted on highground, in cover, I was micromanaging some other group and saw three whole brigades in line on one of the ridges just standing there, jaws slack, as Confederates shot them off by the score. Also multiple incidents that caused immediate, critical defeats.
Example 3: Upon arriving at their destination, brigades will often change their positioning for no reason at all, resulting in horribly skewed firing lanes that, in turn, result in crap along the lines of Example 2. It's not a morale issue, it's like they say, "well. Now that we're here, let's face that river for no reason instead of facing the massive army of rebels coming right at us!" Multiple incidents.
It also seems like there is a terrible imbalance to the Confederates. I'm not talking about historically accurate numbers and the order of battle, I'm talking about the fact that 1 much larger regiment of 3 star (max efficiency) line infantry on the Union side are supposed to be way better than the rebels in sustained ranged combat.
If that's true, then why did they lose to a regiment a third of their size that was standing in an open field down hill? My soldiers had 60% cover behind a stone wall, 100% morale, and 80% condition with their general just behind them. 15 seconds later, they're barrelling off down the opposite side of the hill, totally routed.
Really?
Meanwhile, Confederate AI gets practically unbreakable morale short of a double flank sticking minie balls and/or bayonets in their ears and  up their asses.
Example 4: Sudden unit slaughter and charges. Lost a group of 90/130 cavalry for no reason. Number of men alive dropped extremely rapidly as they were chasing a single, routing enemy with no one firing at them. When I say rapidly, think immediate death of 90 cav in a single second with no source. As for the charges, units seem to be impetuous with no clear reason??? I keep having soldiers cease fire to just...march to the enemy. Not a charge. They just stop what they're doing and start marching to them instead of them attacking. No movement arrow. It's like they've run out of ammo but are noncommitally trying to decide to fix bayonets like men or maybe just commit assisted suicide.
The latter is the only result I've ever seen thus far.
Example 5: Finally, on the subject of "the AI not cheating," I call ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Switched sides, charged 2000 Conf. into a single brigade of 750 skirmishers to test morale mechanics.
Confederates broke morale FROM MAXIMUM and ran, their morale deserting them faster than Kim Kardashian did Kris Humphries.
WHAT?
As Union, the exact same Conf regiment charged and killed all three of the Union skirmish groups as they were all firing down into them. They crossed a river, a forest, and ran uphill.
/end bug examples (adding more every time I try and play this garbage in order to find some redeeming factor)
Time to talk about the stuff that is mechanically functional, but still doesn't actually work.
The game has no idea what elevation is when it comes to units and knows nothing about stacking. Units behind one another can still fire on a target, regardless of elevation and whether or not friendly fire would occur.
In regards to the stacking, as far as I've been able to tell, feel free to clump all your units in one giant glob of flesh and musket. From what little testing I've done of this aspect (can hardly get past all the nonsense), doing so will only result in damage of individual target units. For example, AI clumps together three brigades. Canister shot? No problem! Damage only done to one unit in the clump! The one I'm targeting! Have fun micro-managing your cannons, thus adding to this game's 0/10 ridiculousness. Cover planning is also a joke. Historically, all sorts of cover was utilized during the battle, yet it seems as if very little save forests actually matter. It's also impossible to tell what kind of terrain offers any sort of arbitrary cover. From fences to stone walls to rock outcroppings, the Union utilized their strong defensive positioning at every turn. It's impossible to effectively do that here.
Would write more, but I think I've spent more time hating this absolute kick in my nostalgia-balls than I have actually slogging through it.
TL;DR Controls and unit responses are game ruiningly clunky; poor balancing in terms of faction perks; unspeakably glitchy in bizarre, unsettling ways; absurdly unintuitive compared to nearly isometric line warfare games that already exist. It's like Goat Simulator: 1863 except the bugs aren't SUPPOSED to be there.
I genuinely cannot comprehend what anyone sees in this carnival freak show of a game; will not buy any of their future abortions.

While not the greatest game out, it took me by surprise. I purchased an RPG bundle because of a game in the mix that I thought looked enjoyable, Two Worlds II came with it and the videos looked alright.
I have quite a bit of experience when it comes to RPGs and gaming in general working on developing my own games, software, etc.. over the years. If I could change one purchase I made at full price, I would've pre-ordered this game at full price rather than buy Arcania ( Gothic 4 ) on pre-order; never again from that company. Gothic 4 is one of the worst games, it is so full of bugs that you can't even walk down a small slope because you keep hitting invisible walls that stops you befor letting you continue. Two Worlds II is actually quite refined.
I haven't played it in a while, but I ended up buying it 3 times ( One bundle had the standard edition, and the Pirates DLC, and then I bought another bundle with the Epic edition, then once for a friend because I enjoyed it so much ). I'd buy it again.

This game seems very polished, I may have encountered a bug that I couldn't replicate. Gameplay is smooth, combat is simple when you get used to it, the controls don't feel clunky like Gothic 4 ( where you can spam pick-up and the character does 20 squats before picking up the item and where hitting enemies is a chore ).
I'd rate this to be almost as much fun as Skyrim. The game has plenty of side-quests, twists, and more. I don't recall whether or not I cleared out 100% of the game, but at over 100 hours of time in game says something. The price I paid wouldn't have even gotten me a movie ticket, or a popcorn at the movies, at that was with buying it 3 times; For a game from 2011, it definitely plays quite well.
If you think the price of a few coffees, a movie ticket, or a few soft-drinks is worth it, consider the cost to entertainment value for a game like this and buy it. If you're on the fence about the $20 price-tag, wait until it is on sale ( the bundle sites still have it too at a steal ) but at $10, it is more than worth it.

PROS
-Has a good chain of progression, so you can't just build the best stuff right away.
-There is always something to do, usually a long list of things.
-If you like building complex logistic networks of machines, you'll like it. It's funner than it sounds.
-Spiderbot is awesome, buggy, but awesome.
-The "Build to" function is incredibly useful
CONS
-If you don't like building complex logistic networks of machines, you'll probably hate it.
-It locks up a lot and needs to be restarted.  This happens at least once an hour.
-AI is really stupid.
-Lots of clipping issues.
-There is no pause, so if your base is under heavy attack and you need to go to the bathroom, you can't pause the game.  You have to exit the game completely.
-Help file doesn't give you nearly enough information.
-Inventory sort by type option makes no sense at all.  If I sort by TYPE, I would expect all of my ores to group together, all of my bug parts to group together, all of my machines to group together, but it just seems like the sorting is very random.
-The organization of the crafting menu is very odd. It desperately needs a search feature.
-As you progress, the game gets buggier and buggier until large chunks of the level just won't load at all no matter how long you wait.  At this point the game becomes unplayable, which is really frustrating since I was getting close to beating the game.
OVERALL IMPRESSION
-Overall I really enjoy the game, however I wouldn't recommend buying it until the bugs are fixed.
REQUESTS
-I would like to see hostile monsters in the underground caverns to make exploration more exciting.
-Lower the volume of the power storage cubes by at least 50%. That constant hum gets annoying after a while.
-Make the smaller enemies attack you if you get near them.
-Make it so you can delete the ship wreckage, maybe with the level 2 build gun.

Life is Feudal  is a great example of what a sandbox game should be; you're thrown in without much of anything and leaves you to figure out how to make your way in the world.  It has a full skill system, like you'd expect from an RPG, that allows you to create your own class by choosing to increase the skills you're actually using
The building system allows you to terraform the terrain and then build a variety of buildings, such as houses, guard towers, walls, etc.  You can also dig tunnels, make farms, make massive cities, whatever you want.
The combat system is based on Mount & Blade's, so it's a physics-based system and not just selecting a target and doing damage based on the roll of some metaphoric dice.
This is what a sandbox should be.  In what little time I've spent playing so far (~40 hours,), I haven't progressed very far at all; there's just so much to learn and do,  But is it worth the $40 they're asking In my opinion, yes.  Despite its bugs Life is Feudal truly is already a phenomenal game.

update 11/12/2014
Keeping my review at recomend.
Some new info after my time playing, since i wrote the review i had 100 hours into the game, and now about 430. took my time learning more about the game.
So let's go and see what i have found out.
1. The game has bugs, but thats expected. most are of the annoying type and don't really cause any major issues in the game.
2. Game lag. this is mostly due to the trees and it not being optimized. if you keep setting down like draw distance on trees the lag is manageable. plus the lag spikes but sometimes they are as manageable and sometimes not. again, somthing thats expected in a game this early in development.
3. Servers i have played on a few private servers and had a blast. until they dropped with no warning. which sucks, lost all my and my teams hard work. I'm not normally a online player that gets onto servers so i don't know if thats normal or not.
4. Updates. there has been a couple since i got the game, last one added ability to put furniture where i wanted it. like in the house i built. so that's a plus. and sounds like more animals will be in the next one. so thats another plus.
5. Combat. crossbows suck. the range is ridiculously short and they come before bows. the simplest weapon, the bow should be first., after the sling that is.
5.1 Combat, Swords. now this can be fun, though with the tree lag it can be problematic at times. but once you figure it out it works rather well. take s a bit of time to find that sweet spot. took me many wolves and mooses before i figured that one out.
5.2 Combat Animals. The wolf, it brings a new fear as you run half naked across the sands or in the forests. you learn why humans feared this animal for eons and tried to eradicate it off the face of the planet. freaking things are deadly. until you get some good armour.. then they more of a nuisance. but if you goof, they can still be deadly. as i found out while wearing plate mail armour. wolf hit me in the head and knocked me silly, he then proceeded to chew my intestines like they was spaghetti.
6. Herbalism, the 50,000,000 million combinations thats possible. now this is crucial because you need flux to build the advanced buildings and structures. and flux.. if you're doing it on your own or with just a couple people. can be tedious to get ahold of and time consuming. but the more people you get, the easier it becomes. and if you have other camps willing to trade. then it becomes super easy.
6. Plant Fiber and coops and making of snares. this one i don't much care for in its current state. plant fiber is very time consuming to get. because you only get 1 from each swipe. even with a team of people working with you, its still a chore. especially since if you want to stock your coops to get dung. well you need a ton of snares, and making snares requires a massive, huge load of plant fiber. i think thats the one major issue i have with this game. that and that coops don't really work yet. and the amount of dung you get off it.. is tiny, and tiny dont work if you have a huge farm that requires it.
there is still a fair amount of content not added yet as of this updated review. but i still endorse this game. and i can see it just getting better and better.

Good game with pretty good levels, some of which just fall short due to illogic and invisible walls, but the majority of which are well-designed and flow equally well.  Loading times are another con, but they don't punctuate playtime too heavily.  Perhaps the greatest perk about the game is that it incorporates platforming in a usually non-invasive way, which gives it a suitably retro feel -- also, fun weapon selection: the devestator, freeze ray, and shrink ray all have a nice, cartoony feel to them.
Many none-too-subtle references to pop and gaming culture as well as common fourth-wall jokes to be found both in level design and in dialogue.  Duke's not an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, he's a macho-man, and he's secure enough not to project his insecurities onto those around him.
Good game, good character, but can be damn frustrating and for no good reason.

If you are a Zelda Fan, this is the game for you. Pretty much identical to a Zelda game: Dungeons, Hearts and Containers, Souls (Rupees), and most importantly IMO the concept of using items you get in dungeons to advance through the game and kill the bosses. There's also an element of Portal later in the game as well, so if you like Portal then that is a plus.
My one main criticism is the storyline. There are 5 dungeons, and the vast majority of them involve getting the hearts of the chosen - the story really takes place during the beginning and end of the game aside from meeting Ulthane. Also, I'll mention some items are MISSABLE - particularly all items in the final dungeon.
If you like Zelda, you'll like Darksiders. If you love Zelda, you'll love Zelda. Get this game if you haven't. Now. It's a 9/ 10.

An amazing game for the puzzle/efficiency addicts out there. I've come across from Factorio/Infinifactory, and I'm loving the increased complexity, exploration aspect and the sheer challenge of just getting to the deeper ore deposits and surviving. Taking the automation genre into 3D makes for an amazing game. The UI needs work, but once you get to grips with it, it's surprisingly easy to use. I'm personally not a fan of Minecraft, as I tend to get bored with pure survival/aesthetic building games pretty quickly. This game hits all the areas that I enjoy in one package: Exploration, problem solving, combat, automation, logistics and the challenge of tweaking your factories to improve their efficiency.
The game has been rock solid stable for me and hasn't crashed once in the 50+ hours I've racked up playing, sometimes well into the small hours of the morning. I'm eagerly awaiting a more stable and comprehensive multiplayer experience. I've only just reached T2 ores, but I'll be buying the expansion anyway as a developer this good deserves support, plus I have no doubt it will add greatly to the experience.
